name: exp2-map-probe-results
description: MAP log-lik probes on experiment2 data of many one-change refinements of the Erlang incumbent; most add nothing
metadata:
  type: project
---

None of these helps.
Primes in their own family on top of powers_own_family gained +0.35 nats; it was submitted as primes_own_family_erlang_interval.

Later probes (iter_0 candidate_4_repair_1): learned reliability (stays 0.9, near-duplicate rejected, RMSE 0.0005), log-odds decision distortion (gamma 1.0, bias 0), posterior/likelihood exponents (tau 1.0), Gamma shape (2.08), decade-aligned interval bonus (-0.87, +0.3 LL but RMSE 0.0019 < 0.002 novelty gate) all fail. One-sided thresholds ([1,n], [m,100]) as their own family: +0.85 LL, RMSE 0.011 vs incumbent; submitted as threshold_concepts_erlang_interval. Use scratch/cmp.py there to get the MAP log-lik and the RMSE against the incumbent together.

Raw exp2 data patterns (iter_1 critique, 2026-10-30): no distance gradient among non-members (near 0.42 vs far 0.40), no parity effect, but a shared last digit with every example gives +0.27. Sets with all examples >=50: targets above max get 14% yes (n=35) vs 45% below min, the opposite of threshold extension. Example members get only 62.5% yes. Consecutive trials on different sets agree 0.565 (carryover).

iter_1 candidate_3 (2026-10-30), probes on threshold_concepts_erlang_interval (MAP LL -2245.33): splitting thresholds into "at most"/"at least" families -2245.31 (nothing); powers own family -2245.19; primes own family -2244.85, RMSE 0.0069 — submitted as threshold_concepts_primes_family. Data layout: 10 participants x 450 trials (rows 0-2249 and 2250-4499 are two stimulus batches, 5 responses per cell); per-participant yes-rate matches the model and lag-1 residual autocorrelation is ~0.02, so per-participant bias and carryover terms are not worth adding. Scripts: iter_1/candidate_3/scratch/res.py (residuals by target position).

Decision-rule probes on threshold incumbent (iter_1 candidate_1, 2026-10-30; MAP LL -2245.33): lapse+free guess rate (lapse 0, also 0 on flat-interval exception_rule_family_prior_2), AND rule m^k (k 1.0), soft threshold on membership (-34 nats), OR rule 1-(1-m)^k (k 1.01, +0.015, RMSE 0.0026 on data rows; submitted as any_of_sampled_concepts_endorsement). The wide-interval family (scale ~66) already absorbs guessing.
Big unmodelled signal: per-participant yes rate is bimodal (5 participants ~0.30, 5 ~0.56; 450 trials each, found from trial_index resets). participant_id is hidden in this run, and design/novelty rows have no trial_index, so a participant-bias model can't be scored from stimulus rows alone.

Similarity probes (iter_1 candidate_0): logistic on exemplar similarity exp(-c_digit*[final digit differs] - c_dist*|t-e|/100). Averaging over examples (NLL 3022) beats summing or max (3052); constant rate 3079; tens-digit match adds nothing once distance is in. So pure-similarity models sit about 780 nats of log-lik behind the concept-learning models (-2246). Submitted as average_digit_magnitude_similarity.

Concept-family probes on threshold_concepts_erlang_interval (iter_1 candidate_2, MAP LL -2245.33): extra families added alone — decades, tens digit, repdigits, two-last-digit unions, |tens-units| difference: weight 0, no gain. Extra multiples (10,13..25): +0.14. Digit sum = s (1..18): +0.41, pool RMSE 0.0072 (passes 0.002 gate); submitted as digit_sum_concepts_threshold_erlang. Probe scripts in /tmp/c2p (mk.py adds a family to the incumbent; nov.py gives novelty-pool RMSE).
Pitfall: model.compile_fn(p_yes, inputs=value_vars) with a dict of MAP values gave wrong p_yes; use p_yes.eval({rv: mp[name]}) over free_RVs instead.

iter_1 candidate_4 probes on threshold_concepts_erlang_interval (MAP LL -2245.33): splitting thresholds into lower/upper families (no gain), within-family rule prior ~ size^gamma (gamma 0.03, no gain), example-position recency weighting (rho 0), no participant-level or lag-1 residual structure, calibration by p-bin is near perfect. Per-example evidence weight k^beta (k = number of examples): beta 0.027, +0.87 LL, RMSE 0.0077, sharply peaked (beta ±0.1 costs 5-15 nats); submitted as set_size_amplified_size_principle. Full-interval tensor version (scratch/order.py there) reproduces the grouped incumbent exactly.

iter_1 candidate_5 probes (2026-10-30): incumbent threshold model MAP -2245.33, well calibrated, per-set deviance z=0.67 overall (fits within chance; participants' yes-rates match too, so no individual-difference signal). Powers-own-family + thresholds: +0.14 only. Weber-scaled + thresholds: no gain. Centre-weighted range sampling (density (u(1-u))^kappa within a range) on erlang base: kappa 0.08, +0.52 over base, RMSE 0.008 vs incumbent; LL falls fast for kappa>0.3. Submitted as centre_weighted_range_sampling. Exact per-example likelihood is slow (0.4 s/grad, 1 core, load ~20); Chebyshev-in-kappa precomputed coefficients per (set, interval) brought it to ~0.07 s/grad; grid/cumsum layout was slower than the 5050x100 matmul.

iter_1 candidate_1_repair_1 (2026-10-30): the OR-rule candidate (any_of_sampled_concepts_endorsement) was rejected as a near-duplicate (RMSE 0.0007). The decision rule is pinned to probability matching: fixed OR k=1.3 costs 33 nats, k=2 costs 258. A nested recognition boost for example-member targets goes to r=0. A constant recognition yes-rate for members (0.62) costs 25 nats with pool RMSE 0.061; submitted as recognition_shortcut_for_examples. Members are only 16 of the 512 pool stimuli. Scripts: /tmp/r1/ll.py (MAP LL + pool RMSE for any list of model files; may not persist).

PPC critiques of threshold_concepts_erlang_interval: iter_1 found 0/8 significant (last-digit match effect closest, p=0.11, model over-predicts). iter_2 statistics (2026-10-30): within-batch participant rate SD (obs 0.017, so the 0.30/0.56 split is between the two batches, not within them), within-set lag-1 agreement, slope of yes on position within a set block (targets in a block are shown in ascending order), in-range width slope, small targets below range, near-edge above minus below, recency (last vs first example), round-target contrast.

iter_2 candidate_5 (2026-10-30): centre-weighted ranges + threshold family (thresholds uniform, exempt from width prior and centre weight): MAP LL -2245.40 vs incumbent -2245.33 and centre-weighted -2245.64; kappa falls to 0.04, so the two refinements explain the same signal. Data-row RMSE vs incumbent 0.0027 (borderline for novelty). Submitted anyway as centre_weighted_ranges_with_thresholds. Aggregate residuals by (location of set, target below/inside/above, near/far) are all within a few points.

iter_2 candidate_3 (2026-10-30), probes on threshold incumbent (MAP -2245.33): linear location tilt on bounded-range prior (lam 0.14, +0.04, nothing). Size-principle exponent gamma on magnitude concepts only (in-range lik alpha*w^-g*100^(g-1)+noise): bounded+thresholds g 0.89, scale 50, LL -2245.08 (+0.25), RMSE 0.008; submitted as range_size_principle_strength. Speed: group ranges by (threshold?, width, n_in) and use a per-set batched matmul over the targets actually asked (padded to 35); a gather by cell index (AdvancedSubtensor grad) was the bottleneck. Grad 0.03 s vs incumbent 0.02. Probe scripts /tmp/c3 (may not persist).

iter_2 candidate_4 (2026-10-30), probes on threshold incumbent (MAP LL -2245.33): small-number production bias p(x|h) ∝ x^-gamma (gamma 0.01, LL -2245.33, RMSE 0.0017: dead). Centre-weighted bounded ranges plus uniform thresholds: kappa 0.043, LL -2245.40 (no gain, thresholds and centre weighting do the same job), RMSE 0.0027 vs incumbent and 0.0077 vs centre_weighted. Submitted as centre_weighted_ranges_with_thresholds. Residuals by set size x (below/inside/above/member) x distance band all |z|<1.4, so no structured misfit is left. Probe scripts: /tmp/c4p/probe.py (MAP LL + RMSE for two model files), res.py.

iter_2 candidate_2 probes on threshold_concepts_erlang_interval (MAP -2245.33): weak sampling for all rules (g 0.98, -0.8), for digit families (g 0.97), neighbourhood "within d of an example" concepts (weight 0), ranges with edges only on multiples of 5 (-17 nats), geometric x2/x3 chains (weight 0), small-number output bias x^-beta within concepts (beta 0.01). Size-principle exponent g on ranges+thresholds only: g 0.85, scale 45, LL -2245.38 (tied), RMSE 0.009; g fixed 0.5 costs 11 nats, g 0 costs 52, so g is identified. Submitted as blunted_range_size_principle. Count form (n_inside/n_outside per set x concept, 5095 concepts) makes MAP ~30 s. Biggest per-set misfit: 27,37,67 (targets 70-79 get 11% yes, model 3%).

iter_2 candidate_0 (2026-10-30, exemplar brief): additive-clustering exemplar averaging (sim(t,e) = sum over shared rules/ranges/thresholds of family weight/|c|, normalised by self-similarity, then averaged over the examples; this is the one-example Bayesian posterior averaged across examples) gives MAP LL -2995: better than the digit+distance similarity (-3022) but ~750 nats behind concept learning. So the multiplicative combination of examples across a set is where most of the concept models' advantage comes from. Submitted as shared_category_exemplar_averaging; check takes ~4 min.

iter_2 candidate_5_repair_1 (2026-10-30): centre_weighted_ranges_with_thresholds was already in the set (submitted by candidate_4), so the first try got RMSE 0. Replacement: set_size_amplified_size_principle + primes own family. MAP LL -2244.08 (incumbent -2245.33, set_size -2244.45, primes -2244.85), so the gains roughly add up; beta 0.025; data-row RMSE 0.006 vs set_size and 0.007 vs primes. Submitted as primes_family_set_size_amplified. Probe script /tmp/c5r/probe.py (eval over free_RVs).
**How to apply:** before reusing a refinement idea, check that models/ doesn't already hold it under some name; stacking two independent small gains is a cheap fallback.

iter_2 candidate_2_repair_1 (2026-10-30): blunted_range_size_principle was rejected as too slow AND duplicated range_size_principle_strength (admitted same round), so switched mechanism. Sampling WITHOUT replacement (j-th in-concept example has prob 1/(size-j)), parameter-free, kept incumbent's grouped-by-width layout: MAP LL -2245.12 (+0.2 over threshold incumbent), pool RMSE 0.0084 vs incumbent, 0.009 vs range_size_principle_strength, 0.0056 vs set_size_amplified, 0.0084 vs centre_weighted_ranges_with_thresholds. Smoke check OK (107 s). Submitted as without_replacement_size_principle.
**Lesson:** before a repair, check models/ for a sibling candidate admitted with the same mechanism.

iter_3 critique of without_replacement_size_principle (2026-10-30): statistics were within-set target variance, near-outside rate for tight clusters (obs 0.78), powers-of-2 extension contrast (0.25), primes contrast (0.38), 16,8 vs 8,16 order (obs exactly 0: same targets, same rate), multiples-of-m beyond the span (0.30), wide unstructured sets (0.47), same-last-digit sets with off-rule in-span targets (0.007). Iters 0-2 found 0/8 significant. Batch yes rates are 0.30/0.56 but the 19 shared cells match exactly (0.21/0.21), so the gap comes from the stimuli.
---
name: exp2-pedagogical-sampling-probe
description: Pedagogical (Shafto-style teacher) sampling on threshold incumbent — learned strength goes to 0; fixed full pedagogy loses ~39 nats
metadata:
  type: project
---
iter_2 candidate_1 (2026-10-30): teacher picks x in h with prob ∝ P_L(h|x)^a (learner with the same prior), mixed 10% random. Learned a (HalfNormal or Normal) → 0.012, LL -2245.4 (= incumbent, near-duplicate). Fixed a=1: MAP LL -2284.1 (39 nats worse); flat-prior inner learner with a=1: -2323. Submitted fixed a=1 as pedagogical_teacher_sampling (exploratory).
Speed trick: P_L(h|x) ∝ prior(h)/|h| / Z(x), the prior(h)/|h| cancels in the teacher's normalisation, so teach = M*invZ[x]/(M@invZ)[h]; with count-matrix @ log_example.T and posterior @ M matmuls, 0.09 s/grad for 5302 concepts x 131 sets.
**Why:** pedagogy is ruled out; don't retry the nested version.
**How to apply:** see [[exp2-map-probe-results]] for the other dead ends.

Repair (2026-10-30): the nested version (teacher likelihood depending on the sampled prior) was rejected as too slow (>30 min at target_accept 0.99). Repair fixed the teacher's reference learner at an equal-family prior and Erlang scale 20, so the teacher likelihood is precomputed and grouped by width like the incumbent: smoke fit 200 iters in 107 s, LL about -2358 (around 110 nats worse than the incumbent).
- [Exp2 MAP probes](exp2-map-probe-results.md) — which refinements of Erlang incumbent gain nothing on exp2 data; threshold family worked; novelty RMSE probe; raw exp2 response patterns; concept-family probes (digit sums best); similarity-model probes (mean beats sum, ~780 nats worse than concept learning); centre-weighted range sampling probe + speed tricks; exemplar averaging of single-example generalisation (-2995); range-only size-principle exponent; without-replacement sampling (+0.2)
- [Exp2 pedagogical probe](exp2-pedagogical-sampling-probe.md) — teacher-sampling strength pinned at 0; fixed pedagogy -39 nats; fast teacher-likelihood trick; nested version too slow, fixed-reference repair

"""Refinement of `threshold_concepts_erlang_interval`: the program is believed
never to repeat itself, so examples are drawn from the concept without
replacement.

People do the same Bayesian concept learning over 45 rules, bounded ranges
[m, n] (Erlang prior s * exp(-s / sigma) over width) and one-sided thresholds
([1, n], [m, 100], their own family), with a prior mass per concept family and
10% of examples taken as random draws from 1..100. The one change: the j-th
example a concept contains is one of its members not yet shown, with
probability 1 / (size - j) instead of 1 / size, so sets that use up much of a
small rule or a narrow range favour that tight concept even more strongly and
targets just outside it are rejected more often. No new free parameters.
"""

import numpy as np
import pymc as pm
import pytensor.tensor as pt

NUMBERS = np.arange(1, 101)
ALPHA = 0.9


def rule_concepts():
    rules = {
        "odd": [n for n in NUMBERS if n % 2 == 1],
        "primes": [n for n in NUMBERS if n > 1 and all(n % a for a in range(2, int(n**0.5) + 1))],
        "squares": [n * n for n in range(1, 11)],
        "cubes": [n**3 for n in range(1, 5)],
        "powers of 2, not 32": [2, 4, 8, 16, 64],
        "powers of 2, or 37": [2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 37, 64],
        "even": list(range(2, 101, 2)),
    }
    rules.update({f"multiples of {m}": list(range(m, 101, m)) for m in [3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12]})
    rules.update({f"powers of {m}": [m**k for k in range(1, 8) if m**k <= 100] for m in range(2, 11)})
    rules.update({f"ends in {d}": [n for n in NUMBERS if n % 10 == d] for d in range(10)})
    rules.update({f"contains digit {d}": [n for n in NUMBERS if str(d) in str(n)] for d in range(10)})
    return rules


def family(name):
    if name in ("odd", "even"):
        return 0
    if name.startswith("multiples"):
        return 2
    if name.startswith("ends"):
        return 3
    if name.startswith("contains"):
        return 4
    if name.startswith("powers of 2,"):
        return 5  # gerrymandered exception rules
    return 1  # primes, squares, cubes, powers


_RULES = rule_concepts()
RULES = list(_RULES.values())
N_RULES = len(RULES)
RULE_FAMILY = np.array([family(n) for n in _RULES])
FAMILY_SIZE = np.bincount(RULE_FAMILY).astype("float64")
RULE_MEMBERSHIP = np.array([np.isin(NUMBERS, c) for c in RULES], dtype="float64")
# Bounded ranges [m, n] with 1 < m <= n < 100, and one-sided thresholds [1, n] or [m, 100].
LO, HI = np.array([(m, n) for m in NUMBERS for n in range(m, 101)]).T
THRESHOLD = (LO == 1) | (HI == 100)
INTERVAL_MEMBERSHIP = ((NUMBERS[None, :] >= LO[:, None]) & (NUMBERS[None, :] <= HI[:, None])).astype("float64")
INTERVAL_WIDTH = HI - LO + 1
WIDTHS = np.arange(1, 99)  # widths a bounded range can have
N_PER_WIDTH = np.array([np.sum(~THRESHOLD & (INTERVAL_WIDTH == w)) for w in WIDTHS], dtype="float64")
N_THRESHOLD = float(THRESHOLD.sum())

with pm.Model() as model:
    rule_log_lik = pm.Data("rule_log_lik", np.zeros((1, N_RULES)))  # (sets, rules)

    # all thresholds, and each group's posterior membership of every target (the
    # prior is uniform within a group, so these do not depend on the parameters).
    width_log_evidence = pm.Data("width_log_evidence", np.zeros((1, len(WIDTHS))))
    width_in_concept = pm.Data("width_in_concept", np.zeros((1, len(WIDTHS), 100)))
    threshold_log_evidence = pm.Data("threshold_log_evidence", np.zeros((1, 1)), shape=(None, 1))
    threshold_in_concept = pm.Data("threshold_in_concept", np.zeros((1, 100)))
    row_cell = pm.Data("row_cell", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))
    rating = pm.Data("rating", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))

    # Prior mass of the six rule families, bounded ranges and one-sided thresholds.
    family_weight = pm.Dirichlet("family_weight", a=np.ones(8))
    log_w = pt.log(family_weight)
    # Characteristic width of the Erlang prior over bounded ranges.
    interval_scale = pm.LogNormal("interval_scale", mu=np.log(20.0), sigma=1.0)

    erlang = np.log(WIDTHS) - WIDTHS / interval_scale
    log_per_range = erlang - pt.logsumexp(erlang + np.log(N_PER_WIDTH))

    log_rules = (log_w[:6] - np.log(FAMILY_SIZE))[RULE_FAMILY][None, :] + rule_log_lik
    log_widths = log_w[6] + log_per_range[None, :] + width_log_evidence
    log_thresholds = log_w[7] - np.log(N_THRESHOLD) + threshold_log_evidence
    log_joint = pt.concatenate([log_rules, log_widths, log_thresholds], axis=1)
    posterior = pt.exp(log_joint - pt.logsumexp(log_joint, axis=1, keepdims=True))
    in_concept = (
        posterior[:, :N_RULES] @ pt.as_tensor(RULE_MEMBERSHIP)
        + (posterior[:, N_RULES:-1, None] * width_in_concept).sum(axis=1)
        + posterior[:, -1, None] * threshold_in_concept
    )  # (sets, targets)

    p_yes = pm.Deterministic("p_yes", pt.clip(in_concept.reshape((-1,))[row_cell], 1e-6, 1 - 1e-6))
    pm.Bernoulli("response", p=p_yes, observed=rating)


def _without_replacement_log_lik(examples, membership):
    """Log P(examples | concept) for every concept, the program drawing its outputs
    without replacement: the j-th example a concept contains is one of its members
    not yet shown, so it has probability 1 / (size - j) rather than 1 / size."""
    size = membership.sum(axis=1)
    shown = np.zeros(len(membership))
    total = np.zeros(len(membership))
    for x in examples:
        inside = membership[:, x - 1]
        left = np.maximum(size - shown, 1.0)
        total += np.log(ALPHA * inside / left + (1 - ALPHA) / 100)
        shown += inside
    return total


def _group(log_lik, membership):
    """Log evidence of a group of equally likely concepts and its membership of each target."""
    top = log_lik.max(axis=1, keepdims=True)
    weight = np.exp(log_lik - top)
    total = weight.sum(axis=1)
    return np.log(total) + top[:, 0], (weight / total[:, None]) @ membership


def prepare_observed(rows):
    sets = [tuple(int(x) for x in str(r["number_set"]).split(",")) for r in rows]
    unique = list(dict.fromkeys(sets))
    index = {s: i for i, s in enumerate(unique)}
    interval_log_lik = np.stack([_without_replacement_log_lik(s, INTERVAL_MEMBERSHIP) for s in unique])
    width_log_evidence = np.zeros((len(unique), len(WIDTHS)))
    width_in_concept = np.zeros((len(unique), len(WIDTHS), 100))
    for i, w in enumerate(WIDTHS):
        sel = ~THRESHOLD & (INTERVAL_WIDTH == w)
        width_log_evidence[:, i], width_in_concept[:, i] = _group(interval_log_lik[:, sel], INTERVAL_MEMBERSHIP[sel])
    threshold_log_evidence, threshold_in_concept = _group(
        interval_log_lik[:, THRESHOLD], INTERVAL_MEMBERSHIP[THRESHOLD]
    )
    return {
        "rule_log_lik": np.stack([_without_replacement_log_lik(s, RULE_MEMBERSHIP) for s in unique]),
        "width_log_evidence": width_log_evidence,
        "width_in_concept": width_in_concept,
        "threshold_log_evidence": threshold_log_evidence[:, None],
        "threshold_in_concept": threshold_in_concept,
        "row_cell": np.array([index[s] * 100 + int(r["target"]) - 1 for s, r in zip(sets, rows)], dtype="int64"),
        "rating": np.array([int(r["rating"]) for r in rows], dtype="int64"),
    }

content.text:
The candidate passes the admission check, but I expect it to lose: at its best-fit values it sits about 50 nats behind the current best model.

**The hypothesis (`limited_family_consideration_set`).** People don't search every kind of program on each trial. Each kind comes to mind with its own probability: parity, special sets, multiples, final digit, contained digit, exception rules, bounded ranges and thresholds. People then do Bayesian concept learning only over the kinds they thought of, with each considered kind getting an equal share of the prior. If the kind that best fits the examples doesn't come to mind, they fall back on whichever kinds did. This chance of coming to mind replaces the best model's fixed prior weight for each kind. Everything else matches `without_replacement_size_principle`.

**Check result.** The admission check printed `OK`. Its short single-chain fit (100 warm-up and 100 kept draws, 103 s of sampling, about 7 minutes in total) gave a finite log-likelihood of −2303.6. A single chain can't report R-hat, so convergence is not verified, and novelty against the other models isn't tested by this check.

**Fit before submitting (log-likelihood at the best-fit point; the best model scores −2245.1):**
- **This candidate:** −2299 with the Beta(2,2) priors I used (−2295 with flat priors). People seem to need unequal prior weights across kinds, and making kinds "sometimes not thought of" doesn't do that job. The full fit will probably prune it, though it is a distinct, testable process account.
- **Two other process ideas fit back to the best model exactly, so I didn't submit them:**
  - A working-memory limit, where each example is forgotten with some probability: the fitted retention went to 1.
  - The same come-to-mind mechanism added on top of the existing prior weights: every come-to-mind probability went to 1 (or 0 for kinds whose prior weight is zero anyway), whether shared or estimated per kind.

I've added these results to the experiment's memory notes so later rounds don't repeat them. The three files are in `iter_3/candidate_1/`: `hypothesis.md`, `model_name.txt` and `candidate.py`.
